title: Endpoint Oscillations, Uniform Regularity, and Word Growth at the Parameter ln 2
content: We study the geometric Bernoulli convolution with contraction α = ln 2 and the standard greedy expansion with base β = 1/α. The distribution function at the endpoint is a power times a positive continuous logarithmically periodic function. We prove that this function is nonconstant throughout 2/3 < α < 1/√2, and an integer certificate gives an oscillation ratio greater than 1.005 at ln 2. The optimal uniform interval-mass exponent equals an explicit expression in the exponential growth rate of maximal cylinder overlap. A fully integer grid calculation proves a uniform exponent greater than 0.996. We also obtain a generating function for the greedy language and exponential convergence of its normalized word count, identify the limiting constant with the endpoint value of the invariant density, and prove the nonnegative partition-pressure formula. Existing dimension theorems are applied with their precise hypotheses to the projected and conditional measures. Full measure dimension, uniform mass bounds, bounded density, and the dimension of complete representation fibers are distinguished throughout. No assertion of absolute continuity at ln 2, and no transfer to nonlinear iterative weights, is made.
